mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a tiny house on wheels and a primary-residence tiny home?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tiny house on wheels (THOW) is often classified as a recreational vehicle (RV) and is built to RV standards, making it mobile but not typically permitted for permanent primary residence on private land in many areas. In contrast, a primary-residence tiny home is built on a permanent foundation, adheres to local building codes (like the California Residential Code), and is legally recognized as a fixed dwelling. Zen Tiny Homes specializes in constructing these code-compliant, permanent primary residences.
